bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 11 in `ot::Message::Write`. The prepared vulnerable checkout in the staged ARVO workspace is commit `082c1c79f5a84aeda8eee4f87d9f261089fb9e78`, which is 141 commits earlier than the sample metadata's `vulnerable_commit` (`dff1694fe160be593dea33a7eb604b844190604a`) but still contains the same vulnerable `SendChildUpdateResponse` call site and is the exact source that produced the saved crash. In that staged checkout, the exact 56-byte `radio-receive-done-fuzzer` witness is copied into `otRadioFrame.mPsdu`; the receive path admits it as an MLE Child Update Request and dispatches to `ot::Mle::MleRouter::HandleChildUpdateRequest`. There, `Tlv::GetTlv(aMessage, Tlv::kChallenge, sizeof(challenge), challenge)` copies only 10 bytes into stack local `ChallengeTlv challenge` (the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte challenge field) but preserves the advertised Challenge length 11 in the copied header. `challenge.IsValid()` still accepts that object because it only requires a length of at least 4, and the same branch queues `Tlv::kResponse` for the reply. The reproduced stack shows `HandleChildUpdateRequest` calling `SendChildUpdateResponse(NULL, aMessageInfo, tlvs, tlvslength, challenge)` from the invalid-child / RxOnWhenIdle branch. Inside `SendChildUpdateResponse`, the `Tlv::kResponse` case calls `AppendResponse(*message, aChallenge.GetChallenge(), aChallenge.GetLength())`, so response construction reuses the attacker-controlled TLV header length instead of the clamped 8-byte `GetChallengeLength()`. `AppendResponse` forwards that pointer-size pair into `Message::Append`, and `Message::Write` finally executes `memcpy(..., aBuf, bytesToCopy)` with `bytesToCopy = 11` while `aBuf` still points at the 8-byte challenge array inside stack local `challenge`. ASan reports the resulting stack overread at `message.cpp:569` and identifies `challenge` in `HandleChildUpdateRequest` as the overrun stack object. The fixing commit `f49d8b7b1d33ddc0ef03d0dea822dec83fbb8722` resolves the bug by changing this call site to `aChallenge.GetChallengeLength()`, which caps the copy size at `sizeof(mChallenge) == 8`.

source.description: First project-side parse on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled Challenge TLV into the fixed stack object later overread during response construction.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 56 bytes (sha256 `4b2ace5d51f5c5b29e79cb78ae3a12576c8ecce0a5f8a7f1cc0b39e48a770e0c`). The harness copies it unchanged into `otRadioFrame.mPsdu` and injects it with `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()`. On the reproduced path this frame reaches router-side `HandleChildUpdateRequest()`, where this call copies a Challenge TLV whose stored header length is 11 into stack local `challenge` with `aMaxLength = sizeof(challenge) == 10`, preserving length 11 while storing only the first 8 challenge bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parse preserves the attacker-controlled Challenge length inside `challenge` and stores the fixed-size challenge bytes later referenced by `aChallenge.GetChallenge()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because `ChallengeTlv::kMaxSize == 8`, the copied stack object holds only the 2-byte TLV header plus the 8-byte `mChallenge` array even though the saved ASan trace shows the stored header length later drives an 11-byte read.

root_cause.description: The response builder reuses the incoming TLV header length as the outbound copy size instead of the fixed/clamped Challenge field length.
root_cause.note: `ChallengeTlv::GetChallengeLength()` already clamps to `sizeof(mChallenge)`, and the fixing diff changes this exact call site to use that accessor. Reusing `aChallenge.GetLength()` here is the missing size obligation that makes the later `memcpy()` read past stack local `challenge`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `Message::Write` copies `bytesToCopy` bytes from the forwarded Challenge pointer without checking that the source still fits in the fixed 8-byte challenge field.
sink.note: On the crashing path `aBuf` still aliases the challenge bytes inside stack local `challenge` from `HandleChildUpdateRequest`, and `bytesToCopy` becomes 11. ASan reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 11` here and identifies `challenge` at `mle_router.cpp:2231` as the overrun stack object.

parser_admitted.description: The MLE header has already been decoded as `kCommandChildUpdateRequest`, and because the harnessed instance is in leader/router role, the receive path dispatches into the router-side Child Update Request parser instead of the end-device handler.

fine_trace.note: Source. The Child Update Request parser finds the request's Challenge TLV and copies it into stack local `challenge`. `ot::Tlv::Get()` first reads the TLV header, sees length 11, and then re-reads only `sizeof(challenge) == 10` bytes total, so the copied object keeps header length 11 but contains only the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte `mChallenge` field.

The validity gate accepts the oversized object because `ChallengeTlv::IsValid()` only requires `GetLength() >= kMinSize` (4) and does not enforce `<= kMaxSize` (8). The same branch appends `Tlv::kResponse` to the reply TLV list, so any response sent for this request will echo bytes from the parsed `challenge` object.

The reproduced crash takes the invalid-child branch in `HandleChildUpdateRequest`: the saved stack points at this exact call site, which sits under `if (child == NULL || child->IsStateInvalid())` and `if (mode.GetMode().IsRxOnWhenIdle())`. Because step 2 already queued `Tlv::kResponse`, this call passes the same oversized `challenge` object and the reply TLV list into `SendChildUpdateResponse()`.

Root cause. When the queued reply TLV is `Tlv::kResponse`, the response builder forwards the fixed Challenge field pointer together with the raw TLV header length 11, so the outbound copy size becomes 11 instead of the clamped `aChallenge.GetChallengeLength() == 8`. The fixing diff changes exactly this call site to `aChallenge.GetChallengeLength()`.

`AppendResponse` records the same 11-byte length in the outgoing Response TLV header and asks `Message::Append` to copy 11 bytes from `aResponse`. `aResponse` still aliases the 8-byte challenge array stored in step 1's stack object.

Sink. `Message::Append` forwards `aResponse` and `aResponseLength` into `Write`, and on the first copy iteration `bytesToCopy` becomes 11. `aBuf` still points at the 8-byte `mChallenge` field inside stack local `challenge`, so this `memcpy()` reads 11 bytes from a 10-byte stack object and overruns its end by 3 bytes. The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 11` here and names `challenge` `[80,90)` as the overrun object.

format.contract: Exactly the staged 56-byte witness `11 01 0a 7f 3b 02 f2 12 4d 4c 4b e3 00 15 00 10 04 00 34 7e ff 67 ff 0d 03 0b 1b 63 67 ff 0d 7f 03 04 04 04 10 01 04 0f 09 0b 17 0b 03 04 04 00 09 0b 7f ff 00 00 10 00` (sha256 `4b2ace5d51f5c5b29e79cb78ae3a12576c8ecce0a5f8a7f1cc0b39e48a770e0c`). The harness copies these bytes unchanged into `otRadioFrame.mPsdu`, sets `frame.mLength = 56` and `frame.mChannel = 11`, and calls `otPlatRadioReceiveDone()`. On the witnessed path the frame reaches `HandleChildUpdateRequest()` in the leader/router role, where `Tlv::GetTlv(..., challenge)` stores a Challenge TLV header length of 11 in fixed stack local `challenge`. The invalid-child / RxOnWhenIdle branch then calls `SendChildUpdateResponse()`, which copies 11 bytes from the fixed 8-byte challenge field. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class beyond this exact witness.
